title: "Structural Bioinformatics"

## Preface

This book is a compiled knowledge base, not a monograph tied to one author's research program. The chapters came from on-demand workshops, open courseware, and related notes, then were merged into a single linear narrative. The main public sources are:

- [Structural bioinformatics (EMBL-EBI Training course materials)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/materials/structural-bioinformatics-materials/) (CC BY 4.0), for repositories, quality checks, comparative modeling, function from sequence and structure, complex modeling, and using AI-predicted structures.
- [AlphaFold: A practical guide (EMBL-EBI Training online tutorial)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/alphafold/) (CC BY 4.0), for how AlphaFold works, validation, confidence metrics, database access, and downstream use.
- [Foundations of Computational and Systems Biology (MIT OpenCourseWare 7.91J, Spring 2014)](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/7-91j-foundations-of-computational-and-systems-biology-spring-2014/), for the broader computational-biology framing (sequence and structure analysis, prediction, and related methods) that sits next to the structural focus.

Additional fragments and equations that shaped drafts live under the repository's `mark/` tree: extracted LaTeX and figures kept as local reference snapshots (textbook- and course-style sources) used while writing; they are not redistributed as a standalone course.

The prose was drafted mostly with AI assistance in Cursor: prompts, edits, and fact checks were iterated in the editor; equations, citations, and figures were checked against the LaTeX build. Treat the result as lecture notes with references, not as peer-reviewed curriculum. When something matters for your work, go back to the primary papers and to the courses above.

Figures were taken from the primary literature, documentation, and course PDFs in two ways: by working in Cursor (selecting regions, exporting crops, fixing filenames and `\includegraphics` paths in the LaTeX tree), and by using [Mathpix](https://mathpix.com/) to snip or OCR equations and diagram fragments from PDFs when that was faster than redrawing or retyping. Either route still required checking labels, aspect ratio, and licensing (journal CC-BY figures, supplementary PDFs, and similar) before inclusion.

Stylistically, the target was the tone of Moritz Hardt and Benjamin Recht's *[Patterns, Predictions, and Actions](https://mlstory.org/)*. Define terms, state assumptions, prove or sketch what is needed, and move on to the next idea.

---

This site is the HTML edition of *Structural Bioinformatics*, built from the same LaTeX sources as the PDF (`main.tex` and `chapters/`). Chapters are generated before each render (`python3 website/quarto_gen.py` via `pre-render`).

For the print-oriented PDF, build with `latexmk -pdf main.tex` as described in the repository README.
